request: What did CRS report about Medicare prescription drug price negotiation and its expected savings?

reply.reply:
**CRS reported CBO estimates that Medicare drug price negotiation would lower the federal budget deficit by $25 billion and, by 2031, reduce Part D prices by 8% and Part B prices by 9%.**

- CRS reported CBO estimates that negotiations would lower the federal deficit by $25 billion and lower Part D prices by 8% and Part B prices by 9% by 2031. (R47682, PDF p. 26)
- CRS stated the IRA created the negotiation program, authorizing HHS to negotiate prices for certain single-source drugs in Medicare Part B and Part D. (R47872, PDF p. 2)
reply.reasoning: The most direct CRS estimate found was reported in its October 2024 discussion of the program, citing CBO. A separate CRS report explains that the IRA authorizes HHS to negotiate prices for certain Part B and Part D drugs.
